evals.prompt: Help me visually review https://github.com/meta/pyrefly/pull/5555. The change is buried in argument matching. Keep the Python test beside the Rust state, explain the nested boolean's consumer, and show the successful case and a nonempty tuple-union edge case. Use pinned source links and label reconstructed states.
evals.expected_output: Interactive page pairing Python and compact Rust-like state, with the surrounding control-flow tour, before/after decisions, definition navigation, and evidence limits. Do not claim the historical PR comparison was rerun without doing so.

evals.prompt: Without reviewing a diff, explain why Pyrefly's argument matcher can accept unary(*xs) when xs has type tuple[int, int, *tuple[int, ...]]. Show the Python call, prefix/cursor state, the consumer of the matched bit, and where the checker loses the runtime arity guarantee. Fetch and pin the source revision; distinguish a current observation from the historical example.
evals.expected_output: Root-cause page using the same source/context/trace presentation without a manufactured diff. If current code changed, report that rather than replaying the historical behavior as current.

evals.prompt: Given a Pyrefly narrowing change and its test, build a visual review pairing the Python branches with Rust type-state transitions. Explain the caller contract and show unaffected-path behavior. Use a supplied commit or request the missing change; do not substitute argument matching solely because it is the bundled example.
evals.expected_output: Use the workflow on a different subsystem when inputs are available. If no change/test was supplied, ask for it instead of fabricating a review. Expose feature-owned state and evidence boundaries without assuming the call-matcher fields apply.
